documents.body:
F/u severe rheumatic MS, chronic HF, PAF on warfarin.

Saw cardiology 11/14, letter reviewed: severe rheumatic MS NYHA III, AF at that visit, no med changes. Feels the irregular beating stopped sometime in December, she isn't sure exactly when. No palpitations since. Breathing at her usual: one flight of stairs then she has to slow down, 2 pillows. Home weights 63-64. No bleeding or bruising on warfarin. Taking all meds.

BP 110/78, HR 69 regular, SpO2 98%, wt 63.5.
Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, apical diastolic rumble. No edema.
ECG today: sinus rhythm with LAE. Out of AF.

- PAF: back in sinus on her own. Continue metoprolol succinate 50, warfarin 5.
- Warfarin: INR today, RN to call.
- Rheumatic MS with HF NYHA III: stable. Continue furosemide 40 / KCl 20. BMP.
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months.
RTC 3 months.

ANNUAL PHYSICAL, 53 y/o F

Interval history: no hospital visits this year. AF episode from last fall resolved on its own by January, no recurrence felt. Breathing stable all year: limits on stairs and hills, manages her job without trouble. Two pillows. Home weights 63-64.
ROS: negative for chest pain, palpitations, syncope, edema, bleeding, melena, hematuria, breast changes, weight loss, low mood.

Problems: rheumatic MS (severe) with chronic HF NYHA III; paroxysmal AF; childhood rheumatic fever.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Working full time.

Exam: BP 130/76, HR 83 regular, RR 15, T 37.2, SpO2 98%, wt 64.1 kg.
NAD. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble (known). Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities no edema. Skin no bruising.
PHQ-9: 0.

Prevention:
- Flu shot and updated COVID vaccine today.
- Shingrix complete (Jan, Apr 2023). Tdap 2022. PCV20 2022.
- Mammogram ordered (last 10/2022 normal).
- FIT kit given.
- Cervical co-test due next year.
- CBC today; lipids and A1c normal last year.

A/P: stable. Continue current regimen. INR, BMP, CBC today. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Worse breathlessness.

S: Over the last few months her breathing has gotten clearly worse. The stairs at work are now hard, she has to stop twice. Some evenings she feels short of breath even sitting on the couch. Waking at night gasping and having to sit up, two or three times a week now. Dry cough on and off. Noticed her ankles swollen at the end of the day lately. No chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting. Taking all meds including furosemide every morning; sodium still low. Home weights 62.5-63.5, she hasn't seen them rise.
Last cardiology visit 11/2022.

O: BP 113/82, HR 72 regular, SpO2 98% RA, wt 63.0 kg.
Mildly winded walking from the waiting room. Lungs clear today. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble in left lateral decubitus. No pitting edema at this time of day.

A/P:
1. Rheumatic MS, severe, with chronic HF NYHA III: progressive symptoms. Needs cardiology reassessment and repeat echo. Referral placed back to cardiology, asked for a soon appointment. No medication change for now; she'll call if worse before then. ED for breathlessness at rest that doesn't settle, chest pain, coughing blood, fainting.
2. PAF, regular today. Warfarin, INR today.

conditions.label: Pulmonary hypertension
conditions.note: Secondary to rheumatic mitral valve disease

reports.text:
Transthoracic echocardiogram, cardiology office.
Mitral valve: leaflets thickened and fixed, with only slight diastolic opening. No significant mitral regurgitation. Left atrium: findings consistent with raised left atrial pressure. Aortic valve: normal, no stenosis or regurgitation. Left ventricle: normal size and systolic function.
reports.conclusion: Thickened, immobile rheumatic mitral valve with restricted opening and raised left atrial pressure; no significant MR; normal aortic valve; normal LV size and function.

reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm; left atrial enlargement; right ventricular hypertrophy.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CLINIC NOTE (received 11/05/2024)
Re: Anjali Rahman, DOB 05/03/1970. Visit 11/01/2024.

Reason: reassessment of rheumatic mitral stenosis because of worsening symptoms, referred back by primary care. Her first visit with us since November 2022.

History: Breathlessness that was previously limited to exertion now occurs at rest. Exercise tolerance has fallen further and stairs are difficult. She wakes at night gasping for air. Intermittent dry cough. Recent swelling of both ankles. Negative for chest pain, palpitations and syncope, and she has no orthopnea.
Rheumatic fever in childhood requiring hospitalization; no long-term prophylaxis followed. No history of coronary or lung disease. No alcohol or drug use.

Current medicines: warfarin 5 mg nightly (target INR 2-3); furosemide 40 mg each morning; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once a day; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once a day. NKDA.

Examination: T 36.8 °C (98.2 °F), BP 112/76, pulse 84 and regular, RR 20.
Mildly dyspneic at rest. JVP elevated. Bibasilar crackles, no wheezes. Loud S2. Grade 4/6 low-pitched apical diastolic rumble with her turned left side down, louder with handgrip, with a palpable thrill; no opening snap. Mild bilateral pitting ankle edema.

Echocardiogram today: thickened, immobile mitral leaflets opening only slightly, with evidence of raised left atrial pressure. No significant mitral regurgitation. Aortic valve normal. LV size and function normal.
ECG: sinus rhythm, left atrial enlargement, right ventricular hypertrophy.

Assessment:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, symptomatic, NYHA class III.
2. Pulmonary hypertension secondary to mitral valve disease: loud S2, elevated JVP, RVH on ECG. New diagnosis.
3. Chronic heart failure.
4. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, in sinus rhythm today, anticoagulated with warfarin.

Plan: medications unchanged. Continue warfarin (INR 2.0-3.0 via PCP), furosemide 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, potassium chloride 20 mEq. Sodium restriction and daily weights. Return to cardiology clinic in one year, sooner if needed.

Attending cardiologist
